decided: The deferred leg gains a second grounding path, from outcome events, used only when the in-flight gauge cannot ground it. An entity is in flight at the window end when it has a `deferred` outcome and no terminal outcome (`success`, `failed`, `abandoned`) in scope; its value is the largest single deferred amount per (currency, entity), the same representative rule realized loss uses (ADR-0009). Age is derived without a new query verb: the deferred query is repeated over the nested ranges [lookback, To-2h), [lookback, To-30m), [lookback, To-5m), [lookback, To-1m), [lookback, To), and an entity's bucket is the oldest range its first deferred event falls in — so the SLA-breach and projected-lost arithmetic, the exact count and the oldest-age floor all reuse the existing bucket-floor code unchanged. The lookback is max(2h, the flow's largest SLA deadline) so backlog older than the window start is still seen. Precedence: a metrics backend that returns any biz_inflight_value series (even at level zero) is authoritative and the events path never runs; a metrics backend with no in-flight series, or an events-only backend, falls to events; a backend serving neither stays unavailable exactly as today. The events-derived leg is deterministic evidence with one caveat naming the source and its two limits (age is from the first deferred event; work never recorded as deferred is unseen). Nothing on the wire changes; ValueContext.Deadline stays encoded and stays unread by the engine, recorded as such. The demo's in-flight gauge is produced by replaying the simulation ledger through the real emit.InFlightTracker with a fake clock, replacing testkit's hand-written reimplementation of the tracker's bucketing, and the harness now records the `deferred` outcome at each queue enqueue the way the integration guide instructs a real emitter to.
why: The 2026-09-03 review found the deferred leg — the README's answer to 'delayed money is not lost money' — grounded only by a gauge that a single in-process tracker publishes. In a real service split the enqueue and dequeue happen in different processes, a consumer stall or crash is exactly when the tracker stops publishing, and a Lambda cannot run one at all; the worked webhook example records ResultDeferred on a payments-service 5xx and that outcome reaches nothing. Events survive process death and are already what the realized and customer legs stand on. The nested-range derivation was chosen over a per-group min-timestamp aggregation because the query AST is frozen (v0.1.0) and every shipped querier — memq, sql, cwinsights, gcplogging — plus their conformance suite would need the new verb; five bounded queries per flow cost nothing new. The gauge stays authoritative when present because a tracker that calls Done knows about completions the event stream may show only outside the window. The replay replaces a reimplementation: testkit.InFlightPointsAt re-derived bucketing by hand, so no golden ever exercised the tracker the README promises, and the demo printed 'none in-flight' because nothing published a gauge for it.
cost_if_wrong: If the terminal set is wrong, value shows as in flight that has in fact resolved (or the reverse) — bounded by the window and named in the caveat, and never merged with realized or estimate. If the precedence is wrong, a deployment with both a tracker and deferred events could read the weaker source; the rule is one predicate in one function with a table-driven test per branch. If the replay disagrees with the hand-written derivation, the goldens change, which CI regenerates and the diff shows — that is the proof the change exists to produce, not a regression. The five extra event queries per flow are bounded and only run when no gauge grounded the leg.
alternatives: Add a min-timestamp aggregation (EventAggFirstAt) to the query surface — exact ages, but a frozen-AST amendment touching four queriers and the conformance suite; rejected for this round, remains the right shape if a later flow needs sub-bucket precision.

Read ValueContext.Deadline from the events to compute breach per entity — the event AST returns no per-event fields, so it needs the same amendment; rejected, and the field's unread status is now stated rather than implied.
Make the events path always win when deferred events exist — rejected: a tracker that observed Done knows completions the event window may not, so the gauge is the stronger source when it exists.
A broker-depth in-flight source (SQS attributes, Kafka lag) — a real design question (counts, not money) with its own ADR; left for its own item.
Leave the leg gauge-only and document the gap — rejected by the founder on 2026-09-03 when the review was presented.
scope: engine/deferred.go gains the events-derived path and precedence; engine/deferred_test.go and engine/engine_test.go carry table-driven tests for the precedence, the terminal set, the bucket derivation and the caveat; testkit/querier.go replaces InFlightPointsAt's body with a tracker replay and EventsFromResult/MetricsFromResultAt record deferred outcomes at enqueue; testkit goldens regenerate if the replay differs; examples/demo and README update only if the demo's printed block changes; docs/adr/0019 records the decision; docs/adapters.md, docs/money.md, docs/example-webhooks.md and docs/integration.md state that the deferred leg is groundable from events and what that costs. No wire-format change, no query-surface change, no gate-surface change.
